name: Cet

attributes.attribute: a Connacht warrior of the Ulster Cycle
killer and rival at the champion's portion contest

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cet is a Connacht warrior of the Ulster Cycle. Writers also spell the name Cét, Cett, Ceat, Ket, or Keth. The Irish word means old, ancient, or enduring. His patronymic shifts between Mágu, Mágach, Maga, and Matach across the tales. In the tale of Mac Da Thó's pig he humbles the Ulstermen with a recital of his combat wins. He even emasculates the warrior Celtchar in that list. He seems set to win the champion's portion, but Conall Cernach arrives. Elsewhere Cet hurls Mesgegra's calcified brain ball at Conchobar mac Nessa and leaves the king badly hurt. Conall Cernach later kills Cet in his turn. Connacht's later royal houses claimed Cet as an ancestor in their genealogies.

okr.objective: Cet is the foremost Connacht champion of the Ulster Cycle.
key_results: He bears the variant spellings Cett, Ceat, Ket, and Keth.
At the feast in the tale of Mac Da Thó's pig he shames the Ulstermen with his combat record.
His listed victims include Celtchar, whom he emasculates.
He nearly wins the champion's portion, but Conall Cernach arrives.
He throws Mesgegra's calcified brain ball at Conchobar mac Nessa and wounds him badly.
Conall Cernach kills him in the end.
Connacht's later royal houses claimed Cet as an ancestor.
